item.title: A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture
item.description: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover. — Jinbang Yang — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Exactly solvable Brill waves: explicit gravitational-wave initial data with trapped surfaces
item.description: Vacuum initial data for pure gravitational waves on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (Brill waves) have so far been obtained only numerically. Here a one-parameter family is solved exactly: in toroidal coordinates the constraint separates, and a suitable seed function makes every mode equation hypergeometric. The data are real analytic and asymptotically flat and exist precisely for $k — Piotr Koc — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
item.description: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary. — A. Rod Gover, Jaros\l aw Kopi\'nski, Andrew Waldron — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Dark matter mass fraction in axion stars
item.description: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function. — A. S. Dmitriev, D. G. Levkov, A. G. Panin, I. I. Tkachev — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.description: Author(s): Kotaro Tanaka, Daemo Kang, Naotaka Yoshikawa, Fumiya Sekiguchi, Hirotaka Terai, Takahiro Morimoto, and Ryo Shimano A terahertz vortex beam imprints its orbital angular momentum onto the Higgs mode of a NbN superconductor to open a route to optically manipulate microscopic quantum states using electromagnetic fields. item.title: Scotogenic dark matter from gauged $L_\mu+L_\tau$
item.description: In this work, we introduce the first scotogenic model based on a gauged $L_{\mu} + L_{\tau}$ symmetry whose spontaneous breaking by two units leaves a remnant matter parity $M_P$. The resulting light active neutrinos are of Majorana nature and the lightest electrically neutral state mediating the scotogenic loop is stabilized by $M_P$ and can be identified as a weakly interacting massive particle dark matter candidate. We analyze the phenomenology of a predominantly singlet-like CP-even scalar dark matter candidate and the representative regions of parameter space compatible with the observed thermal relic abundance. The $Z'$ boson is compatible with a broad range of parameters relevant… — J. Echeverria-Puentes, Sergey Kovalenko, Pablo San Martin Sartori, Carlos A. Vaquera-Araujo, Yoxara Villamizar, Jilberto Zamora Saa — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid
item.description: Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its… — Philippe G. LeFloch, Luc Rozoy — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Spherical orbits around a Newman-Janis-generated rotating Bronnikov black hole
item.description: We investigate spherical geodesics in a Newman--Janis-generated rotating regular geometry constructed from the magnetically-charged Bronnikov mass profile. The Kretschmann scalar is exponentially suppressed at the center, and is smooth across the disk and ring within the single-sheeted domain $r\geq0$. We show that all physically admissible spherical photon orbits outside the event horizon are radially unstable in the black-hole regime, whereas stable spherical photon orbits can exist in horizonless configurations. The unstable photon orbits determine the shadow, which for an edge-on observer is smaller and distorted compared with the Kerr shadow. For timelike motion, we identify… — F. Subandi, H. S. Ramadhan — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Massive de Sitter correlators at one loop
item.description: Fermions and massive fields charged under an unbroken symmetry couple to the inflaton only in pairs, so their signals in primordial correlators begin at one loop. Templates for these signals are mostly late-time estimates. Starting from a representation of massive de Sitter correlators as finite Mellin-Barnes integrals, we compute the exact squeezed coefficients of these signals and their corrections away from the squeezed limit. The leading coefficient factorizes into a hard part and a soft vertex. Late-time estimates treat the hard part exactly but approximate the soft vertex by its late-time limit, whereas we compute both exactly. Without a chemical potential, the exact coefficient… — Amara McCune — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Central charges as black-hole hair in weakly coupled trace-anomaly gravity
item.description: We study black holes in Gabadadze's weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, keeping both the Euler and the Weyl central charges. We prove that a constant anomalyon on any Ricci-flat geometry, the Kerr family included, solves the full theory if and only if the two central charges coincide. Otherwise, the black holes continuously connected to this branch carry scalar hair whose charge is fixed by the surface gravity, the horizon topology and the difference of central charges alone: maximally supersymmetric matter leaves black holes bald, the Standard Model and photon-dominated sectors produce hair of definite sign, and conformal collider bounds confine it to a… — Francisco Tello-Ortiz, A. V\'asquez, Kazuharu Bamba, Ghulam Mustafa — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
item.description: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of… — Federico Huxhagen, Diana L\'opez Nacir — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Imprints of perfect fluid dark matter distributions and topological defects on Born--Infeld AdS black hole signatures
item.description: We construct a static, spherically symmetric \BI{} \AdS{} \BH{} that carries a topological defect, either a \GM{} or a \CS{}, and is immersed in \PFDM{}. The metric function collects four independent deformations of the Schwarzschild geometry: a constant solid-angle deficit $(1-\xi)$ from the defect, the nonlinear charge sector controlled by the \BI{} scale $\beta$, the logarithmic \PFDM{} term set by the intensity $\lambda$, and the \AdS{} curvature $\Lambda$. We verify that the solution reduces to the charged \AdS{}--\PFDM{} defect geometry as $\beta \to \infty$ and to Schwarzschild when all deformations switch off. The horizon, photon sphere, and shadow all grow monotonically with the… — Faizuddin Ahmed, Ahmad Al-Badawi, \.{I}zzet Sakall{\i} — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory
item.description: State update rules and their behaviour in Bell tests play an important role in the study of measurement schemes and quantum information. We consider the state updates of the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory using their connection to the probability distribution of measurement outcomes. We focus on a set of observables of the form $A(f_i)^*A(f_i)$, where $A(f)$ is the (complex) smeared field operator for any theory induced by a formally hermitian, Green hyperbolic differential operator, and where the $(A(f_i))_{i=1, \dots, m}$ are assumed to be normal and mutually commuting. Under the assumption that these operators have a sufficiently nice representation on a… — Christopher J. Fewster, Christiane K. M. Klein — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Horizon mergers and initial test-charge acceleration in charged black-hole geometries with anisotropic sources
item.description: We study horizon mergers and the initial radial acceleration of charged test particles in static, spherically symmetric black-hole geometries with a string cloud, a Kiselev power-law component, or a logarithmic profile conventionally. After separating the Maxwell contribution, the effective environmental stress tensors are anisotropic and are not identified with homogeneous quintessence or pressureless cold dark matter. Using a common mass-function formulation, we derive the horizon-merger conditions and classify the Kiselev branches. In this family, the inner-event merger charge provides only an upper bound: three distinct positive horizons can additionally require a positive lower charge… — Saeed Noori Gashti, Mohammad Ali S. Afshar, Mohammad Reza Alipour — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer
item.description: Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening… — El\'eana Berteaux, Florian Nortier — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons
item.description: We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of… — Shiyu Cao — arXiv math-ph / hep-th / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Evolution and Prospects of Higgs Boson Searches Beyond the Standard Model
item.description: The search for Higgs bosons Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) began intensively at the Large Electron-Positron (LEP) collider (1989-2000), continued at the Tevatron (2001-2011), and entered a new era with the start of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in 2010. While the discovery of a Higgs boson in 2012 established the Standard Model mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking, it also opened a wide landscape of open questions that motivate ongoing BSM Higgs searches. This review traces the evolution of these searches across experiments, highlighting both experimental techniques and underlying theoretical ideas in an accessible manner. Emphasis is placed on how different collider environments… — Andre Sopczak — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
item.description: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000… — Vikram Manikantan, Vasileios Paschalidis — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
item.description: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the… — Alireza Maleki — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Beyond the Peak: Constraining early dark energy with the damping tail
item.description: Early dark energy is commonly characterized by the amplitude and location of its primary energy-injection peak. We show that its post-peak evolution, which we call the \emph{EDE tail}, provides an additional observable probe of the underlying scalar dynamics and can materially affect its ability to alleviate the Hubble tension. We construct a simple phenomenological framework in which distinct regions of a multiscale scalar potential govern the dynamics at different field scales. As a representative realization, we consider a potential that combines axion-like and $\alpha$-attractor-like regimes, thereby allowing the EDE tail to be reshaped through reflection and asymmetric oscillations… — Hao Wang, Gen Ye, Yun-Song Piao — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
item.description: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar… — Shin'ichi Nojiri, Sergei D. Odintsov, V. K. Oikonomou, Oem Trivedi — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
item.description: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos. — Matthias R. Gaberdiel, Beat Nairz, Cheng Peng — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Black hole binary mergers in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity with regularisation
item.description: We study the non-linear dynamics of Chern-Simons gravity with numerical relativity for the first time. We use the regularisation prescription to obtain a well-posed initial-value formulation in the gauges commonly used in numerical relativity, and we simulate head-on collisions and binary black hole mergers in the regime of validity of effective field theory, extracting the corresponding scalar and gravitational waves. This opens up the possibility to test general effective field theories of gravity, including those with higher-than-second-order equations of motion, with gravitational waves. — Llibert Arest\'e Sal\'o, Maxence Corman, Pau Figueras, \'Aron D. Kov\'acs, Shunhui Yao — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: ACT Excited: Reconciling Starobinsky and Quadratic Chaotic Inflationary Models with ACT Results via Excited States
item.description: Data Release 6 of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, combined with Planck, CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, favours a higher scalar spectral index $n_{s}$ than Planck and a mildly positive running $\alpha_{s}$, putting the Starobinsky model in tension with the data, while the quadratic chaotic model is already excluded by its large tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. We show that relaxing the Bunch--Davies assumption for the initial state of the scalar perturbations can restore agreement without modifying the inflaton potential. Parametrising the Bogoliubov coefficients by an excitation parameter $\chi_{S}$ and a relative phase $2\varphi_{S}$, we derive the shifts of $n_{s}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ induced… — Amjad Ashoorioon, Abdolreza Yousefi-Sostani — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
item.description: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schr\"odinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using… — Nikola Herceg, Tajron Juri\'c, A. Naveena Kumara, Andjelo Samsarov, Ivica Smoli\'c, Kumar S. Gupta — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
item.description: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schr\"odinger pictures through state--operator duality. Using a gravitational charge as a quantum clock, we construct a modular crossed product with density operators whose trace entropy reproduces generalized entropy up to clock… — Feng-Li Lin, Sayid Mondal — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Symmetry breaking Poincar{\'e}--Einstein metrics and non-extendable boundary Killing fields
item.description: We construct Poincar{\'e}-Einstein metrics on $R^2xS^3xS^2xS^2$ which bifurcate from anti-de Sitter black holes whose horizon is the product of a B{\"o}hm metric on $S^3xS^2$ with a round $S^2$ , and which break the rotational symmetry of the $S^2$ factor while keeping their conformal infinity. Some Killing fields of the conformal infinity therefore do not extend to the bulk, although $$\pi$^1(M, $\partial$M ) = 0$. item.title: Near-boundary and near-horizon momentum--Krylov response in noncommutative-inspired BTZ spacetime
item.description: We compute the proper radial momentum of a massive probe falling into a Lorentzian-smeared, noncommutative-inspired BTZ black hole at fixed asymptotic mass, and use it as the growth rate of momentum--Krylov complexity. In the BTZ limit the accumulated complexity is $\mathcal{K}_0 = X(\cosh\tau - 1)$. With smearing, the initial growth coefficient is $F'_\alpha(X)/4$, while the late-time exponent is the surface gravity $F'_\alpha(x_+)/2$. The two depend differently on the smearing parameter, so the deformed response is not a rescaled BTZ curve; we show this analytically and confirm it numerically. For a distant release point the early response approaches BTZ, whereas the late-time rate does… — F. A. Brito, F. G. Costa, J. A. V. Campos — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Quadratic-in-spin scattering of compact bodies at fourth post-Minkowskian order
item.description: We present the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin at arbitrary velocity and mass ratio. We include spin-induced quadrupoles and radiation reaction, supplemented by curvature-squared spin-tidal terms. Three-loop worldline integrals yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. Infrared poles cancel exactly, fixing the tail logarithm. We obtain a new post-Newtonian coefficient and third-order angular-momentum loss for general quadrupoles. The new input shifts resummed predictions for black-hole scattering. — Taushif Ahmed, Syed Mehedi Hasan — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Void inside the horizon: connecting the third-quantized vacuum to a classical spacetime
item.description: We investigate the emergence of a classical spacetime from a quantum-gravitational vacuum within the framework of third quantization applied to the black hole interior. Following the canonical quantization of the Kantowski--Sachs spacetime, one can construct a wave packet that explains the classical interior of a Schwarzschild black hole. This wave packet should be extended to the classical singularity. To avoid this, one can introduce an analytic continuation and the Euclidean wave function. This is not an analytic continuation of the spacetime, but of the superspace. To give this a suitable meaning, it is reasonable to introduce the concept of the third quantization. In this aspect, the… — Dong-han Yeom — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Primordial black holes production in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
item.description: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter. — Ekaterina O. Pozdeeva, Sergey Yu. Vernov — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Boundary spectroscopy of hidden near-horizon reflection
item.description: A classical black hole horizon absorbs completely, and any deviation would be hidden in the bulk. For a scalar field in a rotating Ba\~nados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior, we derive an exact boundary response of a corotating passive wall near the horizon. An Airy filter gives its spectrum, and positive energy excludes growing modes. On any frequency band the response identifies a constant wall impedance and the wall position, which enter orthogonally with weights determined by the spectral function. The boundary thus sees a reflecting wall, whereas a perfect absorber is exponentially hidden. — Yiling Chen, Jiayue Yang, Zhen Zhong, Robert B. Mann, Jie Jiang, Ming Zhang — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
item.description: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass… — Nikola Savi\'c, Filippo Vernizzi — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Chiral and deconfinement thermodynamics of the Polyakov-quark linear sigma model with and without charm quark: an SU(3) versus SU(4) comparison
item.description: Using the Polyakov-loop extended linear-sigma model (PLSM), we investigate strongly interacting matter at finite temperature and baryon density by comparing the three-flavor (u,d,s) and four-flavor (u,d,s,c) formulations on equal footing, with the aim of isolating the thermal contribution of the charm quark. The model describes chiral dynamics through explicit and spontaneous symmetry breaking and reproduces the vacuum spectra of scalar and pseudoscalar mesons. Confinement is incorporated through a logarithmic Polyakov-loop potential calibrated to the continuum lattice-QCD equation of state (EoS). Within the mean-field approximation, we calculate light-, strange-, and charm-quark… — Nourhan M. Rfeek, Hossam Wahid, Fatima M. Rfeek, Alexandra Friesen, Yuri Kalinovsky, Saleh O. Allehabi — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Rotating Black Holes from Scaling Transformations in Horava Gravity
item.description: We study the scaling transformations that change the physical parameters of solutions in low-energy Horava gravity. In particular, we present a simple scaling transformation that generates rotating black-hole solutions in low-energy Horava gravity from known relativistic solutions. As explicit examples, we obtain "Doran-like" and "Kerr-Schild-like" rotating solutions in Horava gravity. We find that both solutions are horizon-penetrating, but their null horizons are not Killing horizons. We also find that, although their singularity structures differ from each other, chronology is protected in both solutions, as in the previously obtained Kerr-like solutions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates. — Deniz O. Devecioglu, Mu-In Park — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: The index from a super-point
item.description: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT. For the… — Dhanvarsh Annamalai, Hyunook Hur, Thomas Hussel, Monica Jinwoo Kang, Craig Lawrie, Jaewon Song — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
item.description: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar… — Armin Hatefi, Ehsan Hatefi — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
item.description: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first… — Karthik R., Shamant Shreedhar Dixit, K. M. Ajith, Kartheek Hegde, Shreyas Punacha, A. Naveena Kumara — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
item.description: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the… — Waqas Ahmed, George K. Leontaris — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
item.description: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples. — Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: $\mu$- and $q$-extension of special functions in quantum field theory
item.description: Analytic calculations up to single-scale quantities in perturbative quantum field theory result into special numbers and functions, which are generalizations as iterative integrals over special alphabets. In this way one obtains polylogarithms, Nielsen integrals, the iterated integrals over linear denominator terms, cyclotomic letters, letters induced by quadratic forms, and square-root valued letters. The inverse Mellin transform relates special nested sums to these quantities, which are harmonic sums, generalized harmonic sums, nested sums implied by quadratic forms, cyclotomic harmonic sums, and nested sums containing central binomials. We construct the $\mu$- and $q$-extensions of all… — J. Bl\"umlein, A. M. Gavrilik, U. Y. Lunha, O. Mykhailiv, C. Schneider — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Constraining Regular Black Hole Models with the Effective Field Theory treatment of General Relativity
item.description: In this paper, we present a method for using perturbative predictions from treating general relativity as an effective field theory to constrain non-perturbative approaches to quantum gravity in black hole contexts. We start by reviewing a known result from this framework, which estimates the first quantum corrections to the interaction energy of a static particle near a black hole. We then propose a way to test non-perturbative quantum black hole models - specifically those formulated as modified Schwarzschild metrics, also known as regular black holes - against this perturbative result. To illustrate, we apply our method to the Hayward metric, showing that it does not align with the… — Sami Viollet — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
item.description: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an… — Lillian Santos-Olmsted, Rebecca K. Leane, Carlos Blanco, John F. Beacom — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
item.description: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)\rho(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. Using appropriate theoretical arguments, the successful galactic scale dark matter model is generalized to have a universal equation of state of the form $\langle P(\chi)\rangle =\langle \rho(\chi)\rangle \langle \sigma_{DM}^2\rangle$, where $\chi$ is the scale of the system under… — V. K. Oikonomou — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
item.description: A stable particle that couples only through gravity is pair-produced in collisions of runaway bubble walls by graviton exchange. For a transition of duration $1/\beta$, a Dirac fermion reaches the yield $Y_X\simeq6.8\times10^{-3}(H/\beta)(T_{\rm reh}/M_{\rm P})^3$, where $H$ is the Hubble rate of the vacuum energy, $T_{\rm reh}$ the reheating temperature and $M_{\rm P}$ the reduced Planck mass. The yield is flat up to masses near $(H/\beta)M_{\rm P}/\nu^2$, where $\nu$ of order one sets the wall-field excursion. Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about $10^{17}$~GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails. — Cheng-Wei Chiang, Van Que Tran — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: The chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory: partition functions beyond large-$N$ and quantum holography
item.description: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. High-precision data support closed forms for their all-order perturbative $1/N$ expansions. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. We also study the three-sphere partition function numerically in the 't Hooft limit and Cardy limit, and propose an all-order Airy formula. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography. — Xuao Zhang — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations
item.description: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation… — Kimberly K. Boddy, Jeffrey S. Hazboun, Kris Pardo — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Effect of dark matter and scalar-cut potential on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars: A chiral quark mean field approach
item.description: We investigate the effects of fermionic dark matter (DM) and scalar-cut potential ($U_{\text{cut}}(\phi)$) on the equation of state (EOS) and macroscopic properties of neutron stars. The baryonic matter consists of neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons under the $\beta$-equilibrium and is described within the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model. In this framework, quarks are confined within baryons, whose properties are modified through the exchange of scalar fields $\sigma$, $\zeta$, and $\delta$, and vector fields $\omega$ and $\rho$. The DM is modelled as a self-interacting fermionic fluid with scalar $\varphi_D$ and vector $V_D^\mu$ mediators. The baryonic and DM fluids… — Hrishika P, Arvind Kumar — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Geometric distinguishability of two-source gravitational-wave signals from the extrinsic geometry of the single-source waveform manifold
item.description: Overlapping gravitational-wave signals can produce strong degeneracies in which a multi-source waveform is accurately represented by a single effective source. We formulate this source-confusion problem geometrically by treating the family of single-source waveforms as an embedded manifold in the noise-weighted detector Hilbert space. We introduce the distance-to-manifold statistic, defined as the minimum residual obtained by fitting a waveform with the single-source model, and show that its squared value is directly related to the maximized likelihood difference between two-source and single-source hypotheses in the noiseless limit. For two sources with nearby parameters, perturbative… — Cezar Valentin Ionescu, Paul Adrian Gog\^{\i}\c{t}\u{a}, Laurentiu Ioan Caramete, Ana Caramete — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Flavor-resolved screening length of a moving quarkonium in a lattice-calibrated holographic QCD plasma
item.description: We compute the screening length \(L_s\) of a moving heavy quark-antiquark pair in a lattice-calibrated Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton background for pure-glue, two-flavor, and \(2+1\)-flavor matter. Parallel and perpendicular orientations are considered at finite temperature, baryon chemical potential, and rapidity. \(L_s\) decreases monotonically with \(T\) and \(\eta\) in every flavor sector, and for the flavored systems also with \(\mu\). The perpendicular screening length is systematically smaller than the parallel one. At zero density and \(T=0.3\ \mathrm{GeV}\), the ordering \(L_s^{(N_f=0)}>L_s^{(N_f=2)}>L_s^{(N_f=2+1)}\) holds in this calibration, and a lattice check of the static flavor… — Huwei Zhu, Zi-qiang Zhang — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Vector boson scattering in composite Higgs models
item.description: Vector boson scattering is a powerful tool to test the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. We focus on Composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description and assume that only one pseudo Nambu-Goldstone boson contributes to electroweak symmetry breaking, which we identify as the Higgs state of the Standard Model. In these scenarios, LHC data imply lower bounds on the predicted resonances below 2 TeV depending on the scenario. Using $WZjj$ production as a benchmark, we demonstrate that the tails of various distributions nevertheless show significant deviations from Standard Model predictions. This holds in particular for the case of longitudinally polarised vector bosons. — Rosy Caliri, Manuel Kunkel, Werner Porod — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
item.description: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN)… — Jezreel C. Castillo, Christopher Munna, Zachary Nasipak, J. David Brown, Charles R. Evans — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Optical appearance of a non-commutative black hole surrounded by an accretion disk
item.description: We investigate the optical appearance of a non--commutative Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a transparent, geometrically thin emitting disk. A Lorentzian matter distribution supplies the effective exterior metric. We compute photon trajectories, disk transfer functions, and the observed bolometric intensity for static and circular emitters, taking into account gravitational redshift, orbital time dilation, and Doppler modulation. At fixed asymptotic mass, increasing $\theta=\Theta/M^2$ from zero to $0.03$ reduces the critical impact parameter by approximately $16.1\%$ and the innermost stable circular orbit radius by $23.7\%$. The narrow higher-order features follow this… — Adailton Azev\^edo Ara\'ujo Filho, Narges Heidari, Alesandro Ferreira dos Santos, Shahin Mamedov, Valdir Barbosa Bezerra, Amilcar Rabelo de Queiroz — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Exact stress-tensor fluctuations from conformal symmetry and black hole radiation
item.description: Semiclassical gravity is sourced by the expectation value of the stress tensor, and it is reliable only if the fluctuations around this value are small. In two dimensions, conformal symmetry captures the essential physics of Hawking radiation in its s-wave sector and determines the mean value exactly, for any background and any quantum state. We show that it also determines the local fluctuations of the null components $T_{\pm\pm}$. The square of the stress tensor is defined by the operator product expansion, up to a multiple $\alpha$ of $\partial_\pm^2T_{\pm\pm}$ that labels point-splitting prescriptions. Its transformation law under the conformal map to locally inertial coordinates gives… — Jos\'e Navarro-Salas, Roberto Balbinot, Alessandro Fabbri — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Lyapunov Stability of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by the Kiselev Anisotropic Fluid
item.description: We investigate the geodesic structure and the stability of circular orbits around a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a Kiselev anisotropic fluid, characterised by the equation-of-state parameter $\omega$ and the normalisation parameter $N$. We consider six representative values, $\omega=-1,-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3$ and $1$, over the admissible range of $N$ determined by the horizon structure, including the corresponding extremal limits. Using the effective potentials for null and timelike geodesics, we determine the photon sphere, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and the outermost stable circular orbit (OSCO), and examine their stability through coordinate-time Lyapunov exponents… — Saswati Roy, Paramita Debnath, Shubham Kala, Hemwati Nandan — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
item.description: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and… — Jialiang Shao, Andrea Addazi, Xinran Wang, Guanwen Fang, Yi-Fu Cai — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Accuracy, Convergence and Consistency of Dark Matter Evolution with the PhotoNs-3 Code
item.description: We systematically investigate the accuracy and convergence of PhotoNs-3, a cosmological N-body code employed for the HyperMillennium simulation. In particular, we examine its convergence with respect to parameters that affect the accuracy of the force calculation and the time evolution, such as the softening length and the adaptive time-stepping scheme, and find that it converges very well. Furthermore, using GADGET as the benchmark, we design four sets of simulations to compare the mutual consistency. We compare the power spectrum of the density field, halo density profiles, and the halo and subhalo mass functions. The difference between PhotoNs-3 and the Gadget codes is at the same level… — Xiaoyang Zhang, Ming Li, Qiao Wang, Liang Gao — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: A note on Holographic Renormalization for Polarized IKKT
item.description: We construct a boundary counterterm for the on-shell action of type IIB supergravity solutions dual to vacua of the polarized IKKT matrix model. The construction is based on the variational principle, with off-shell fluctuations whose fall-off conditions are based on the asymptotic equations of motion. The renormalized on-shell action of the supersymmetric saddles reproduces the matrix- model result once we pass to the ensemble of fixed D1-brane charges, which we implement off-shell by dualizing the RR two-form potential. — Matteo Guglielmetti — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Closure of averaged Einstein equations by DESI data
item.description: We benchmark the hypothesis that the redshift dependence of postulated dark energy in the standard model, measured by the DESI collaboration, is a natural outcome of dark energy-free models of structure formation in general relativity. We recall fundamental results and the properties of averaged dust cosmologies that suggest to replace the dark energy equation of state through the nonperturbative impact of the inhomogeneous geometry. The relevant mechanism can be phrased in terms of an effective mean field description of inhomogeneities using the fluid analogy of a scalar field (the `morphon'). Without violating energy conditions this effective field exhibits a cross-over to phantom… — Thomas Buchert — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Bounds on entanglement fluctuations at holographic interfaces
item.description: How small can entanglement fluctuations be at fixed entropy? For a class of holographic conformal interfaces supported by a scalar with a potential, we prove $c_\text{eff}\leq c_\text{cap}\leq c_\text{eff}^2/c_{LR}$, relating entropy, capacity, and energy transmission. The coupled gravitational response is a transport term minus a positive scalar contribution; the background Einstein equation bounds that subtraction. A long Janus throat allows unbounded capacity at a finite entropy coefficient while the scalar response remains gapped. — Pallab Basu, Vishnu Jejjala — arXiv math-ph / hep-th
